subject: gk
question: What was the recommendation of the Narasimham Committee-Il regarding public sector banks?

options.text: Reduce lending by public sector banks
Increase government ownership in public sector banks
Merge and consolidate public sector banks

solution:
The correct answer is __**Merge and consolidate public sector banks**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Narasimham Committee-II, constituted in 1998, recommended the **merger and consolidation of public sector banks** to create fewer but stronger banks.
 
• The aim was to improve **operational efficiency**, enhance competitiveness, and address the challenges posed by globalization and financial sector reforms.
 
• The committee suggested **reducing the number of public sector banks** to around 3-4 large banks with international reach and a few regional banks.
 
• It emphasized that consolidation would lead to better capital adequacy, stronger balance sheets, and increased capacity for funding large projects.
 
• The recommendation was part of a broader agenda to reform the banking sector and make it more robust and prepared for future economic challenges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Narasimham Committee Reports:**

 
 
• The Narasimham Committee was constituted in two phases: Narasimham Committee-I (1991) and Narasimham Committee-II (1998).
 
• The first committee focused on liberalization and deregulation of the banking system.
 
• The second committee emphasized structural reforms, including consolidation, governance improvements, and non-performing asset (NPA) management.
 
 
 
• **Public Sector Banks:**
 
 
• Public Sector Banks (PSBs) are banks where the majority stake is held by the government.
 
• They play a critical role in financial inclusion and economic development in India.
 
• Examples include the State Bank of India (SBI), Punjab National Bank (PNB), and Bank of Baroda.
 
 
 
• **Bank Consolidation in India:**
 
 
• In recent years, the government has implemented the consolidation of PSBs, such as merging Bank of Baroda with Dena Bank and Vijaya Bank.
 
• In 2020, 10 PSBs were merged into 4 large banks to create stronger entities.
 
• Consolidation aims to improve efficiency, reduce redundancy, and strengthen the overall banking system.
 
 
 
• **Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):**
 
 
• CAR is a measure of a bank's capital relative to its risk-weighted assets.
 
• The Narasimham Committee-II emphasized maintaining adequate CAR to ensure financial stability.
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) mandates a minimum CAR as per Basel norms for all banks.
